weeks.note: Week 2: に vs で. Short and slow first (a ticket window, a first trip, a hotel), then a longer travel episode and one NHK show for the composer in you.

picks.title: S1E6 - 駅で: 切符を買います
picks.source: Small Talk Café - Learn Japanese in Minutes
picks.why: Five minutes at a ticket window, the same exchange as your Trains scene. Short enough to play twice in a row: once cold, once after the prep words.
picks.connection: This week's に vs で at the station: 駅で for what you do there, 熊本に / まで for where the train goes.
picks.listenFor: Every time you hear a place, catch the particle after it. で → something happens there (buying, waiting). に or まで → that's where someone is going. Say place + particle out loud.

picks.title: マルクスがはじめて日本に行きました 1 /4(Markus's First Trip to Japan 1/4)
picks.why: You finished one of Noriko's stories last week. This is a four-part first trip to Japan, so you can do a part a day and finish the set.
picks.connection: A first trip is all に and で: flying to a city, arriving at a hotel, eating somewhere — this week's pair in story form.
picks.listenFor: Follow the story by its に's: each one is a place Markus goes to or ends up at. Then catch one で and say what he did there.

picks.title: #1588「ホテルで使う日本語について！」
picks.why: Front-desk Japanese, told slowly by a host you already know. A preview of the inn check-ins on your rail loop.
picks.connection: Hotels are where に vs で lives: going into your room, eating breakfast on a floor, waiting in the lobby. Same pairs as this week's review.
picks.listenFor: When you hear 部屋, フロント or a floor number, catch the particle after it: に (going or being there) or で (doing something there)? Then say one sentence of your own about an inn.

picks.title: Vol.483 【陸・海・空】東京から5,000円($30USD)でどこまで行ける？ (Japanese Radio for Listening practice)
picks.why: How far 5,000 yen gets you from Tokyo by rail, bus, sea and air. Trip planning in natural speed, right before your own rail loop. Long, so take it in 10-minute pieces.
picks.connection: で as "by means of": by train, by bus, by boat. How you travel takes で; where you end up takes に or まで.
picks.listenFor: Each time a new way of travelling comes up, listen for the で right after it. Then catch the place it reaches and its に or まで, and say your own: 〇〇で〇〇に行きます.

picks.title: 現代の音楽「現代音楽 100年のレガシー71 武満徹 2」
picks.why: Part two of two on Takemitsu: a composer you know well, discussed in Japanese on the contemporary-music show. Aired Sunday Oct 11, repeated Saturday morning. NHK's catch-up stream may be region-locked; the link is the October listing.
picks.listenFor: Don't try to follow it all. Every time you hear 曲 or 作曲家, catch the particle right after it (は, が, を, に, で) and guess what's being said about the piece.

weeks.note: Week 1: は vs が. Start with the Teppei episodes. Try each one once with no transcript before you look anything up.

picks.title: #1587「レストランでの日本語について！」
picks.why: Short, slow and all about the situation you'll be in most: walking into a restaurant and ordering. It's the easiest way to start hearing restaurant Japanese without subtitles.
picks.connection: Matches the Ordering food scene, which gets its natural tier (この店は何が有名ですか) this week.
picks.listenFor: Listen for は and が after food words. は = "as for the ramen…" (talking about it). が = "the ramen is the one…" (picking it out). Pause after each one you catch and say which it was.

picks.title: #1589「日本に来て使う日本語について！」
picks.why: Teppei goes through the Japanese a visitor actually uses after landing. That's the same "want to say it, then say it" loop you run on a trip.
picks.connection: Trip prep: the phrases someone needs in their first days in Japan, at about the level of the Survival tiers.
picks.listenFor: Each time Teppei starts a new topic, listen for the noun + は that introduces it. That's the frame for everything that follows. Count how many topics you hear.

picks.title: #643「新しいレコーディングのシステムとか、チャーハンとか！」
picks.why: Teppei talks through a new recording setup, then the conversation moves to fried rice. It's gear talk and food talk between two people, which is how chats at a bar tend to go.
picks.connection: Recording gear is everyday work for you, and that vocabulary will come up in Itoshima.
picks.listenFor: In a two-person conversation, が often shows up right after a question: 何が…? → Xが…. Every time one of them asks a question, listen for whether the answer starts with が.

picks.title: #124 Tokyo vs Rural Japan – A Winter Walk in My Village
picks.why: Native speed, about 12 minutes, and there's a free transcript. A winter walk through a village in a small rural place, set against Tokyo: that's close to the move you're about to make.
picks.connection: This is contrastive は, the other job は does in this week's lesson.
picks.listenFor: Compare sentences: when Imari says 東京は… and 村は…, は is setting up a contrast between the two places. Catch three pairs.

picks.title: #118 What to Say When You Don’t Understand Japanese
picks.why: At native speed, but the topic is the escape hatch you'll need at a bar: what to say when you don't understand. Each phrase you pick up here keeps a conversation going.
picks.listenFor: Write down any phrase she gives that you'd actually say. Then listen for the word right before each は or が in it, and ask whether it's a topic or a pick-out.
